title: Potato, canned, fat added, NS as to fat type

content.title: About
content.content: Canned potato with added fat is a ready‑to‑eat product obtained by boiling or steaming potatoes and then preserving them in oil or with added vegetable fat. It is often used as a quick side dish or an ingredient in various recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning allows the potatoes to be stored for 2‑3 years without refrigeration.
Added fat enhances flavor and increases the caloric value of the product.
In some countries, canned potatoes with oil are a traditional field‑rations food for hikers and military personnel.
Canned potatoes are frequently seasoned with salt and spices to boost taste.
The technology for canning potatoes was developed in the early 20th century.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The combination of fat and carbohydrates provides a quick source of energy, especially useful in limited‑food situations.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Potatoes retain vitamin B6 and niacin, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Canned potatoes contain potassium, supporting normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Thermal processing makes the potatoes soft and easy to digest, suitable for people with chewing difficulties.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Frequent consumption may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Canned products often contain significant amounts of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: Some individuals may react to the oils used in the product.

items.title: Bacterial contamination if the can is damaged
items.content: Compromised packaging can allow pathogenic bacteria to grow.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned potatoes can be eaten cold in salads, heated in the microwave, or added to soups, stews and casseroles. They are convenient to dice and use as a base for quick meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer the contents to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for no more than 3‑4 days.
